title.narrative: Early lifesaving emergency WASH services to communities projected to be most affected by El Nino induced riverine flooding in Jowhar.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspangtInternational Medical Corps (IMC) is a US-registered independent affiliate organization of International Medical Corps UK (IMC UK), with which IMC UK shares the same name and charitable objectives and mission. IMC UK and IMC work together to deliver assistance programs in an accountable and effective manner to pursue their commonly held charitable objectives. IMC UK will engage IMC to implement its programs in the field, with IMC UK oversight, according to the terms and conditions of the agreement that results from this proposal and the terms of the party’s administrative service agreement. Together with IMC Croatia, IMC provides administrative and operational support to IMC UK and the programs on the ground, including but not limited to financial management, banking and cash management, procurement management/international procurements, and logistics.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtThis project aims at reducing morbidity and mortality related to disease outbreaks and acute malnutrition as a result of El Nino-induced riverine flooding through improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene facilities to the targeted vulnerable populations in Jowhar. The project will cover 6 months starting 1ltsupgtstlt/supgt November 2023 to 30ltsupgtthlt/supgt April 2023. The project will target to reach 14,000 direct beneficiaries (9,720 from host communities and 4,280 IDPs) and 137,291 indirect beneficiaries. IMC seeks to create awareness to facilitate adoption of proper hygiene and sanitation practices, enhance community engagement and empowerment activities ownership of the project, improve water-point infrastructure to increase sustainability and access of safe water, and facilitate uninterrupted access to sanitation facilities resilient to climatic shocks.ltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltbrgt
ltpgtltspangtTo achieve this, IMC proposes to conduct emergency water trucking to 300 families (1800 individuals) among the displaced riverine communities at the historic Airport IDP site and Daifa villages, ltspangtrehabilitate two public boreholes at Mahaday and Dabaylay villages, rehabilitate one shallow well at Gumbe village,lt/spangt construct two 50-cubic meters concrete elevated water storage tanks for Mahaday and Dabaylay boreholes to benefit 10,000 beneficiaries, perform pipeline extensions with installation of water kiosks for Dabayley village and Airport IDP, establish and train 18-member Water Management Committee to enhance active linkage between IMC and the community, conduct routine mass chlorination of water sources at the proposed rehabilitation water-points, construct of 80 gender segregated latrines ltspangtwith hand washing facilitieslt/spangt and solar lamps targeting 2400 beneficiaries, install access ramps, sitting potties and handrails to 12 latrines (15% of the constructed VIP latrines), for the elderly, pregnant women and ltspangtPWDs for ease of access and usage, conduct regular desludging for the inundated latrines in targeted locations adversely affected by El Nino-induced floodslt/spangt, establish and train 14 community hygiene promotion volunteers (8 men, 6 women) to conduct routine mass household hygiene promotions, procure and distribute 1,000 hygiene kits targeting the most vulnerable El Nino flood affected IDPs and Jowhar riverine villages, conduct community cleanup campaigns twice every week to make sure the IDPs and surrounding Jowhar riverine village environments are kept clean from solid waste, and facilitate feedback and accountability mechanisms through an established CBFRM Accountability to Affected Populations structure comprisingltspangt lt/spangt(i) community dialogue and consultation meetings for WASH project setup (ii) sensitization and training of CBFRM AAP for community committees (iii) development of local CBFRM and AAP materials by a hired artist.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspangtIMC targets ten implementation sites identified to be most at risk of adverse effects of flooding including IDP sites and Jowhar riverine villages as follows: (1) Alla amin IDP (2) Alla suge IDP (3) Gumbe (4) Blook (5) Da'ifo (6) Bulowaray (7) Dabaylay (8) Airport IDP sites (9) Shamiindo (10) Mahaday.lt/spangtlt/pgt
